title: Coefficient extension of local Frobenius through the specified point comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb/\Ql$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$, with geometric Frobenius as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. All coefficient categories are the raw rationalized constructible categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and Weil pairs and their morphisms are those of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Use the specified natural pullback-composition and pullback/scalar comparisons, rationalized with their equality-of-morphisms and finite-iteration compatibilities, of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization].

Let $F\subset L$ be finite subextensions of $\Qlb/\Ql$, write $T_U(M)=M\otimes_F L$ on $U=X,s$, and write $T_{\mathrm{pt}}(C)=C\otimes_F L$ on ordinary point complexes. Let $n\geq1$ and $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ with geometric point $\bar x:s\to X$. For $H=F,L$ put $P_H=L\bar x_H^*$, $Q_H=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,H}$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $D_H=Q_HP_H$, $G_{H,r}=L(g_X^r)_H^*$ and $S_{H,r}=L(g_s^r)_H^*$. Let
$$a_{r,M}:T_XG_{F,r}M\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{L,r}T_XM$$
be the specified pullback/scalar comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with normalization as above. Write
$$b_M:D_F(M)\otimes_F L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_L(T_XM)$$
for the inverse rationalized point-sections scalar comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] followed by $Q_L$ of the specified pullback/scalar comparison for $\bar x$. For a Weil pair $(M,\theta)$ over $F$, put $M^T=T_XM$ and $\theta_L=T_X(\theta)a_{1,M}^{-1}$. Use the iterated Weil maps and point transports of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] and [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural]. For $H=F,L$ let
$$\rho_{H,N}:S_{H,n}P_HN\xrightarrow{\sim}P_HG_{H,n}N,\quad R_H(N)=Q_H(\rho_{H,N})I_{P_HN}^{[n]},$$
where $\rho$ uses $g_X^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$.

The maps $b_M$ are natural isomorphisms for all morphisms of $D^b_c(X,F)$: for every $v:M\to M'$,
$$b_{M'}(D_F(v)\otimes_F L)=D_L(T_Xv)b_M.$$
For every $F$-Weil pair $(M,\theta)$ their iterated structure maps satisfy
$$\theta_L^{[r]}a_{r,M}=T_X(\theta^{[r]})\quad(r\geq1).$$
For every $M\in D^b_c(X,F)$ the return transports satisfy
$$D_L(a_{n,M})b_{G_{F,n}M}(R_F(M)\otimes_F L)=R_L(M^T)b_M.$$
The local operators $\mathcal F_{H,x,n}(N,\eta)=D_H(\eta^{[n]})R_H(N)$ therefore satisfy
$$b_M(\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(M,\theta)\otimes_F L)=\mathcal F_{L,x,n}(M^T,\theta_L)b_M.$$
All assertions apply to the full constructible Weil-pair domain, with no integral Weil-stable lattice or finite-Tor condition on finite reductions. For $F=L$, $b_M$ is the identity under the specified unit identifications.

proof.text:
Write $V=T_{\mathrm{pt}}$ and let $u_N:VQ_FN\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_LT_sN$ be the inverse rationalized sections comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Its naturality says $u_{N'}VQ_F(w)=Q_L(T_sw)u_N$. Write $e_M:T_sP_FM\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LT_XM$ for the specified pullback/scalar comparison for $\bar x$. Its naturality, from [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] with the choices of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], says $e_{M'}T_sP_F(v)=P_LT_X(v)e_M$. Since $b_M=Q_L(e_M)u_{P_FM}$, substitution gives
$$b_{M'}VD_F(v)=Q_L(e_{M'})Q_L(T_sP_Fv)u_{P_FM}=D_L(T_Xv)b_M.$$
Both factors of $b_M$ are isomorphisms, so this proves the first assertion.

proof.text:
Use the iterated-map convention of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Let $c_{H,r}:G_{H,r+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{H,r}G_{H,1}$ be the specified compositor. The mixed equation and finite-iteration clause of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] give
$$c_{L,r,T_XM}a_{r+1,M}=G_{L,r}(a_{1,M})a_{r,G_{F,1}M}T_X(c_{F,r,M}).$$
Prove $\theta_L^{[r]}a_{r,M}=T_X(\theta^{[r]})$ by induction. For $r=1$ cancel $a_{1,M}^{-1}a_{1,M}$ in the definition of $\theta_L$. If it holds for $r$, expand $\theta_L^{[r+1]}=\theta_L^{[r]}G_{L,r}(\theta_L)c_{L,r,T_XM}$ and substitute the displayed mixed equation. As $\theta_La_{1,M}=T_X\theta$, naturality of $a_r$ at $\theta:G_{F,1}M\to M$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta_L^{[r+1]}a_{r+1,M}
&=\theta_L^{[r]}G_{L,r}(T_X\theta)a_{r,G_{F,1}M}T_X(c_{F,r,M})\\
&=\theta_L^{[r]}a_{r,M}T_X(G_{F,r}\theta)T_X(c_{F,r,M})\\
&=T_X(\theta^{[r]}G_{F,r}(\theta)c_{F,r,M})
=T_X(\theta^{[r+1]}).
\end{aligned}$$

proof.text:
Apply the final coefficient-extension assertion of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization] with $E=F$, its $M=L$, $m=n$ and $y=x$. Its $J_{y,H}$ is $D_H$ here. Its $t_{y,n,M}$ is exactly $R_H(M)$: both are the $n$ successive point transports followed by the return comparison for $g_X^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$ in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. The lemma writes the target as $D_H(G_{H,1}^nM)$; identify $G_{H,1}^n$ with $G_{H,n}$ by the specified compositors. Its iterated scalar map $d_M$ then becomes $a_{n,M}$ by the finite-iteration coherence of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Its $b_M$ is our $b_M$: both use the specified pullback comparison and inverse sections comparison (moving the latter past the former is precisely its naturality in step 1). Thus the lemma's displayed scalar equation reads
$$D_L(a_{n,M})b_{G_{F,n}M}V(R_F(M))=R_L(T_XM)b_M,$$
which is the required return equation. The cited lemma assumes separated finite type and rational constructibility, and explicitly imposes no finite Tor-amplitude condition.

proof.text:
Apply step 1 to the actual rational morphism $\theta^{[n]}:G_{F,n}M\to M$. Use step 2 and then step 3 to calculate
$$\begin{aligned}
b_MV(\mathcal F_{F,x,n})
&=D_L(T_X\theta^{[n]})b_{G_{F,n}M}V(R_F(M))\\
&=D_L(\theta_L^{[n]})D_L(a_{n,M})b_{G_{F,n}M}V(R_F(M))\\
&=D_L(\theta_L^{[n]})R_L(T_XM)b_M
=\mathcal F_{L,x,n}b_M.
\end{aligned}$$
The first and last expressions use the local-operator definition of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. This is the claimed intertwining identity.

proof.text: All equations above are in the raw rationalized categories of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. In particular step 1 applies to all their morphisms: the integral naturality equation is linear, so after scalar localization it holds on each $f\otimes\lambda$ and hence on their sums. The same applies to the mixed comparison equation. A Weil structure in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] is only a rational isomorphism; $\theta_L=T_X(\theta)a_{1,M}^{-1}$ is again an isomorphism, and step 2 uses its rational naturality without choosing an integral Weil-stable lattice. Step 3 already holds on the full constructible domain. Finally, for $F=L$, [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] makes $u_N$ the identity under the stated unit identifications and [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] makes $e_M$ the identity. Therefore $b_M=Q_L(e_M)u_{P_FM}=1$. No restriction on the Tor-amplitude of finite reductions entered any step.
